text: dsh-composer-input-history 是面向 DSH Web 会话编辑器的输入历史插件，在会话编辑器停靠区注册不可见组件，并监听上下方向键。按上键可从当前会话找回已发送的文本，继续向上浏览更早输入；按下键可向新消息前进、恢复浏览前的草稿，再按一次可清空。历史按会话保存最近 300 条，并与当前聊天记录合并；打开菜单、输入法组合或编辑器状态不适合接管按键时会让编辑器处理。适合希望在 Web composer 中重用提示词并找回未完成草稿的人。代码未读取外部 API key 或调用外部服务。

dsh-composer-input-history adds arrow-key recall to DSH Web sessions. Press Up to browse sent messages; press Down to move forward, restore your draft, or clear it. It keeps up to 300 entries per Session in localStorage and yields when menus or IME composition own the keys.
想用上下方向键翻看当前会话之前发过的输入。
上键找回旧提示词，下键回到我刚才正在写的草稿。
I want to recall earlier messages from the current chat composer with the arrow keys.
dsh-composer-input-history 的功能「会话输入历史」：在 DSH Web 会话编辑器按上键逐条找回已发送文本，按下键前进并恢复浏览前的草稿，再按下键可清空。历史最多保留每个会话最近 300 条，并与当前聊天记录合并。
dsh-composer-input-history 的功能「按键与草稿协调」：在会话编辑器监听方向键，只在可安全接管时更新草稿；菜单、输入法组合、编辑中的多行光标等情况由原编辑器继续处理。

dsh-composer-input-history README · dsh-composer-input-history：Shell-style input history for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web composer — the behaviour you know from opencode and other terminal agents.

> Press <kbd>↑</kbd> in the composer to pull back a message you already sent in this Session.
> Press <kbd>↓</kbd> to walk forward again; past the newest message your original draft comes back,
> and one more <kbd>↓</kbd> discards it and clears the composer.

dsh-composer-input-history README · What it does：| Gesture | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> with an empty draft | recalls the newest sent message |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> again | walks one message older each time |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> on the first line of a single-line draft | recalls; the draft you were writing is remembered |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> inside a multi-line draft, below the first line | left to the editor, so the caret still moves |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> while browsing | walks one message newer |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> past the newest message | restores the draft you were writing before browsing |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> again, after the draft came back | discards the draft and clears the composer |
| typing anything while browsing | leaves browse mode; the recalled text becomes your draft |

dsh-composer-input-history README · What it does：History is what you sent in this Session, oldest to newest, read from the Chat node store the view itself renders (`snapshot.nodes`, ordered by anchor sequence): ordinary user messages, steering messages, and the message that woke a turn. Skipped: hidden nodes (compacted or interrupted), attachment-only messages, and everything the Harness authors on your behalf — goal rounds, skill catalogs, runtime snapshots, job notices, model notices, approval answers, and compaction checkpoints. The visible window is also persisted per Session in `localStorage` (capped at 300 entries) and merged with the live store, so messages a compaction pruned stay recallable, including after a restart.

dsh-composer-input-history README · Why it is a keyboard observer：The Harness composer deliberately leaves <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> to its shell-owned Lexical editor, so no slot or command seam owns them. This plugin therefore:
section: Why it is a keyboard observer
Why it is a keyboard observer

text: dsh-composer-input-history README · Why it is a keyboard observer：Replacing a draft commits paragraph by paragraph, so intermediate empty or partial drafts are expected; the plugin treats a published draft that matches what it wrote (ignoring whitespace) as its own and keeps browse mode. Only a genuinely visible slash/reference menu (a mounted `role="listbox"`), an IME composition, or a held modifier keeps the key — a caret move the editor already marked as handled does not. Editing keys (Backspace, Delete, Enter, printable characters, <kbd>Ctrl+V</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl+X</kbd>) end browse mode; navigation keys and shortcuts such as <kbd>Ctrl+C</kbd> do not. The browse state machine itself is cached per composer editor element, so re-rendering or remounting the dock entry never drops the browse state or the remembered draft, and starting browse again from an already-recalled message never overwrites the draft you were writing — walking past the newest message always lands on that draft, a blank composer included. text: dsh-composer-input-history README · Why it is a keyboard observer：A key is declined when an open menu owns it, when an IME is composing, when a modifier is held, when the event is outside the composer editor, or when the composer is submitting/adjudicating. The plugin imports no Harness Client package and styles nothing.

dsh-composer-input-history README · Install：From npm (short form):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-input-history
```

Or straight from this repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/liumorrisclaw/dsh-composer-input-history
```

You can also add it in the Web UI's **Plugins** page, or list the package directory with the plugin manager. The bundle ships off until the profile selects it.

For a local checkout, install by path:

dsh-composer-input-history README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-composer-input-history
```

dsh-composer-input-history README · Relationship to other plugins：The npm name `dsh-input-history` is already taken by a different community plugin that also recalls prompts with <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd>. The two differ in mechanism and behaviour:

dsh-composer-input-history README · Relationship to other plugins：| | dsh-composer-input-history (this plugin) | dsh-input-history |
| --- | --- | --- |
| History source | the Session transcript the Chat view already loads | a separate local store of submitted prompts |
| Non-empty draft | recalls and remembers the draft, restoring it below the newest message | recalls only from an empty composer |
| Attachments | not part of the recalled text | persists and re-attaches them |
| Menu/IME | yields the key to an open slash/reference menu and to IME composition | — |
dsh-composer-input-history README · Relationship to other plugins：Pick this one if you want recall driven by the conversation you can see, including from a draft you are already typing.

dsh-composer-input-history README · Compatibility：Developed and verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.2.0-rc.2`. The plugin uses only documented seams: `ctx.slots`, the Session standard props (`useChat`, `useInput`, `inputActions`), `ctx.shortcuts.observeFixedInput`, and the activation context's `uiSession` binding source (declared in `dsh.client.inject`). It declares `dsh.client.inject` on `dsh-client-ui-conversation`, `dsh-client-ui-chat`, and `dsh-client-shortcuts` so activation order is deterministic.

dsh-composer-input-history README · Verified：- 48 tests (`npm test`): 40 unit tests over the pure history reader, the browse navigator, and keystroke arbitration, plus 6 simulated-composer integration tests that mount the real bundle against a stub React host and stub DOM — whole-draft publish, the stale-draft refill and its counter-punch, compaction pruning merged with the persistent record, manual edits, menu yields, and IME declines.
- The composed profile contains the bundle row (`dsh --profile <name> --dump-config`).
- The browser boot graph announces the bundle with its inject list and `immediately: true`, and the web host serves the bundle body byte-for-byte.
- End-to-end in a real harness Web instance driven over the DevTools protocol: the dock entry mounts in a session composer, <kbd>↑</kbd> recalls the sent message, walking down lands on the draft and a further <kbd>↓</kbd> clears it, a typed draft survives rapid up/down walks, and the console stays clean.
- Recalling a message with <kbd>↑</kbd> was confirmed by hand in a running Desktop composer.

dsh-composer-input-history README · Limitations：- History is per Session. Cross-session recall (recent Sessions' inputs) is not implemented yet.
- History reflects the loaded transcript window plus the persisted per-Session record; a message never seen by this plugin (sent while it was uninstalled) is not recalled.
- The recalled text is plain text: reference chips and attachments from the original message are not restored.
- One resident composer per Web page is assumed, matching the shell's own design.
- On the home screen (no Session open) there is no recall: the composer dock only renders inside a session.
